original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 5.18 Real-time a: To determine the binding strength of QP11, real-time biomolecular interaction analysis with Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) was carried out at physiologically relevant concentrations by using AutoLab Esprit SPR (at Advanced Instrumentation Research Facility, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, India). Kinetic rate constants: Ka and Kd (association and dissociation rate constants, respectively) as well as affinity constant, Kd were measured at room temperature (RT, 293 K). SPR analysis was performed by following previously described protocols [57–62]. Briefly, 25 μM each of FP2 and FP3 were immobilized on the surface (self-assembled monolayer of 11-Mercapto-undecanoic Acid, MUA on gold surface) of SPR sensor chip by the mechanism of covalent amine coupling. The chemistry involves covalent linkage of esterified carboxyl groups of the sensor surface with ε-amino group of lysine residues of a given protein. Unreacted ester groups on the sensor chip surface were blocked with 10 mM Ethanolamine, pH 8.5. Interaction kinetics was studied by injecting QP11 at different concentrations: 3.125, 6.25, 12.5, 25, and 50 μM (for the interaction of QP11 with FP2); and, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, and 100 μM (for the interaction of QP11 with FP3), over the FP2- and FP3-immobilized SPR sensor chip surface, respectively, followed by comparing their respective kinetics and binding affinities at RT. Interaction of FP2 with E64 (1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, and 15 μM), a known falcipain inhibitor [32], served as positive control. A control flow cell was activated and blocked in a similar manner with the injection of equivalent concentrations of DMSO to allow for reference subtraction. PBS was used both as an immobilization and binding buffer. Data were fit to the two-state conformational change model using AutoLab SPR Kinetic Evaluation software provided with the instrument. Kd value was calculated using the Integrated Rate Law (IRL) equation: R(t) = E.(1-e^(-kobs*t)) + R(0) eq. (3) Where E is the maximal extent of change in response at a certain concentration and is equal to Kd.C.Rmax/(Ka.C + Kd); Ks is equal to (ka.C + kd); and R(0) is the response unit at t=0. E and Ks were evaluated at each concentration by minimizing the residual sum of squares between observed data and the model equation using Solver in MS Excel. Evaluation of Kd at four different concentrations of the compounds was done to calculate Kd according to the following equation: Kd = ka.C + kd eq. (4) Where Ks is a concentration-dependent parameter that is dependent upon ka and kd. The ratio of intercept (ka) and slope (kd) of the above line was ascertained to be the dissociation constant or Kd.
original_paragraph.Results - 2.2.8 Surface Plasmon Resonanc: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) is an optical technique employed to detect molecular interactions, wherein, the binding of an analyte to a ligand molecule immobilized on a thin film changes the refractive index of the film. Consequently, the angle of extinction of light alters when polarized light is incident on the film, which is monitored as a shift in the detector position that corresponds to the dip in reflected intensity. To quantify the interaction of QP11 with FP2 and FP3, SPR analysis was performed using AutoLab Esprit SPR. The proteins were immobilized on the sensor chip surface, where they remained stable throughout the experiment. Interaction analysis was done by injecting serial dilutions of QP11 onto the FP2 and FP3-immobilized sensor chip surfaces and comparing their respective kinetics & binding affinities at RT. With an increase in the mass concentration of QP11, a gradual increase in sensor signal was observed, which directly correlated with the corresponding change in the refractive index of the medium immediately adjacent to the SPR sensing surface. Concentration-dependent real-time sensorgrams as well as Kd values for the interaction are shown in Supplementary Figure S5 (H). QP11 showed differential binding affinities for FP2 and FP3, with Kd values of 1.4 x 10^-5 M and 7.4 x 10^-5 M, respectively. Notably, for the interaction analysis of QP11 and FP2, the calculated ka (or, kon; association rate constant) and kd (or, koff; dissociation rate constant) values were determined to be: 680.4483 ± 431.1045 M^-1s^-1 and 0.0974 ± 0.0111 s^-1, respectively. Whereas, for the interaction analysis of QP11 and FP3, the calculated ka and kd values were determined to be: (-1.6700 ± 0.8632) E4 M^-1s^-1 and 0.3048 ± 0.0730 s^-1, respectively. original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. In vitro evaluation of QP11 interaction with FP2 and FP3. A. Evaluation of QP11 interaction with FP2 and FP3 using MST. The thermophoretic mobility of fluorescently labeled FP2 and FP3 showed significant alterations, indicating effective interaction with QP11. The dissociation constants (Kd) were determined as 2.99 ± 1.91 μM for FP2 and 54.4 ± 3.8 μM for FP3. B. In vitro enzyme inhibition assay to evaluate the hydrolysis of fluorogenic peptide Z-Phe-Arg-AMC by FP2 and FP3 in the presence of QP11. (i) Line-weaver Burk plot using 5 μg enzyme and varying concentrations of the substrate (Z-LR-AMC) in the presence of different concentrations of QP11. (ii) Plot correlating apparent Km values with varying QP11 concentrations, resulting in a Ki value of ~0.527 μM. The in vitro enzyme assay with QP11 demonstrated differential inhibition of falcipains activity, supported by in silico docking and MST-based interaction analysis.
